claims.title: Precedent: turbulence multifractals cracked by thermodynamic formalism from operator algebras
claims.statement: Intermittency's anomalous exponents were not derived from Navier-Stokes directly; they became tractable when Ruelle's thermodynamic formalism - developed for operator algebras and smooth dynamical systems - was imported by Frisch and Parisi (1985) to describe turbulent signals as a 'free energy' over singularity strengths. A phenomenological but rigorous counting framework replaced direct dynamical attack.

claims.title: Precedent: enzyme reaction rates cracked by Kramers' physics barrier-crossing theory
claims.statement: Kramers' 1940 theory of thermally activated barrier crossing - formulated for Brownian particles in physics contexts - became the standard quantitative framework for biochemical reaction rates, protein conformational transitions, and enzyme turnover. Enzymology's rate problem was absorbed by importing a physics diffusion model, not by biochemical theory developed internally.

axis_texts.semantic: Biochemical rate problems were absorbed by a physics diffusion-over-barriers model built decades earlier for other purposes.
axis_texts.mechanism: model reaction as particle escaping a free-energy well under friction; friction regime determines rate law
axis_texts.math_structure: Kramers turnover Fokker-Planck free-energy barriers transmission coefficients
axis_texts.problem_shape: attribution problem partially dissolved by a universal rate framework
axis_texts.failure: Kramers framework needs a known free-energy surface; attribution inside the surface remains open

claims.title: Precedent: mutation-load limits in evolution cracked by information-theoretic error thresholds
claims.statement: Eigen's quasispecies error threshold imported Shannon-style coding theory into molecular evolution, yielding the first quantitative ceiling on information accumulation under mutation. This telecom-mathematics formalism reorganized the sex/recombination debate around information maintenance rather than gene-level fitness bookkeeping.

axis_texts.mechanism: model genome as message under noisy channel; error threshold bounds maintainable information
axis_texts.math_structure: error threshold quasispecies channel capacity mutation-selection balance
axis_texts.problem_shape: cost-benefit debate reframed as information maintenance capacity
axis_texts.failure: threshold models assume sharp peak landscapes; real fitness landscapes soften the conclusions

claims.title: Precedent: anesthesia onset modeled as a statistical-physics phase transition of cortex
claims.statement: Anesthetic induction was recast by Steyn-Ross and colleagues (2001 onward) as a phase transition in stochastic neural field equations - importing the criticality/phase-transition toolkit from statistical physics into anesthesiology. The move converted 'which molecule' questions into 'which bifurcation' questions and predicted hysteresis-like endpoints later sought in EEG data.

axis_texts.problem_shape: many-to-one convergence recast as universal transition phenomenology
axis_texts.failure: mean-field models idealize cortex; transition signatures in data remain debated

claims.statement: The invariant-discovery problem was transformed when Cousot and Cousot (1977) imported order theory - complete lattices, Galois connections, Tarski fixed-point theorems - into program analysis as abstract interpretation. 'Find the invariant' became 'compute the fixed point of a monotone function on a lattice', trading exactness for soundness by design.

claims.title: Precedent: dynamic-programming lower bounds cracked by communication complexity
claims.statement: Barriers against subquadratic dynamic programming were made rigorous by importing communication complexity - a framework born in distributed computing (Yao 1979; Aho-Hirschberg-Ullman applied it to DP table size). The observation that two players holding the two strings must exchange quadratically many table entries became the template for modern fine-grained lower bounds.

axis_texts.math_structure: communication complexity reductions set disjointness matrix rigidity
axis_texts.problem_shape: impossibility proofs via information exchange lower bounds
axis_texts.failure: communication reductions give conditional bounds; unconditional barriers remain out of reach

claims.title: Precedent: extremal set theory cracked by the entropy method from information theory
claims.statement: Several extremal set-system problems were cracked by the entropy method: Radhakrishnan's entropy proof of Bregman's theorem, entropy proofs of LYM-type inequalities, Shearer's lemma as a counting engine. The pattern - replace combinatorial bookkeeping with information inequalities - is the established import route Frankl's conjecture has not yet surrendered to, which is itself informative.

claims.title: Precedent: glass transition theory cracked by mean-field spin glass mathematics
claims.statement: The leading microscopic theory of the structural glass transition - Random First-Order Transition theory - came from importing mean-field spin glass mathematics (Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model, Parisi replica symmetry breaking) into supercooled liquids (Wolynes and collaborators). A magnetism formalism supplied the ideal glass transition, configurational entropy, and mosaic predictions.
